purpose: Prevent a successful revision/evaluation/learning loop from collapsing project-specific range, character distinction, productive irregularity, or multidimensional craft into a repetitive optimized style.
rules: All drift thresholds are relative to project/book baseline, clean controls, holdouts, or explicit protected traits rather than a universal great-prose target.
One soft homogenization signal requires review; multiple independent soft signals retain the original by default.
Hard identity-collapse risks reject the candidate even when another dimension improved.
Intentional irregularity is defended only when it is actually protected by project/user evidence; novelty or irregularity is not automatically good.
Repeated optimization of one dimension is risk evidence, not proof of failure by itself.
Named-author targets and universal prose scores are forbidden.
Missing clean-control or project-holdout evidence fails closed rather than silently passing.
